events.continuity_hook: This narrows the Seattle summit plan after the initial comparison of arrival day, hotel area, local transportation, and possible weekend extension.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the Wednesday outbound, settle the work-night hotel, decide whether to hold a flexible weekend room, and outline seat, airport-transfer, and meeting-arrival steps before booking.
events.scenario_brief: The Seattle vendor lab is confirmed for Wednesday at 4:30 p.m., so Erin is leaning toward the Wednesday afternoon nonstop from Denver rather than risking a Thursday morning arrival. The conference block is closest to the South Lake Union sessions but has limited wellness amenities, while the Lake Union hotel has stronger fitness access, a pool, and better weeknight availability but no listed hot tub. Her spouse is still checking whether he can join Friday night, so Erin needs a booking path that secures the work stay without overcommitting the weekend.

events.continuity_hook: This follows the Seattle work-stay decision and turns the optional spouse weekend into a real lodging and flight choice.
events.interaction_goal: Decide whether to stay at the Lake Union hotel or split hotels for the weekend, pick the spouse flight and Sunday return timing, and identify any room-change, luggage, and local-transport steps tied to that choice.
events.scenario_brief: Erin's spouse can now join Friday through Sunday, but the conference block no longer has Saturday availability and the Lake Union hotel can only extend the stay if Erin accepts a room-type change after Friday. A waterfront boutique property near Pike Place has a balcony room and strong reviews for the weekend, but it lacks a pool and hot tub and would require moving after the final summit session. His Friday evening Denver-to-Seattle nonstop arrives late enough that light rail plus a short rideshare may be simpler than adding a rental car.

events.continuity_hook: This is the final practical check after the Seattle summit booking and spouse-weekend extension were settled.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm the itinerary still works, then organize weather planning, airport transfers, hotel arrival, meeting timing, spouse arrival, seats, and carry-on packing.
events.scenario_brief: Six days before Seattle departure, Erin has the Wednesday afternoon nonstop, the Lake Union hotel from Wednesday through Sunday, her spouse's Friday evening nonstop, and the Sunday return booked. Rain and wind are likely during the summit window, and a downtown event could slow South Lake Union rideshares on Friday evening. The hotel will store Erin's bag if the room is not ready before the vendor lab, but she still needs to confirm the lab check-in window, spouse airport pickup plan, seat selections, compact conference-and-weekend packing, and whether light rail is still the best airport strategy.

events.continuity_hook: This starts the next client-training episode after the Seattle conference travel wraps up.
events.interaction_goal: Build a ranked first plan for arrival day, flight routing, hotel zone, rental car, demo-case handling, and the client confirmations Erin needs before booking.
events.scenario_brief: After the Seattle summit, Erin is assigned a late-March diagnostics rollout across the Research Triangle, with a likely Monday setup in Cary, Tuesday and Wednesday clinic trainings in Durham and Raleigh, and a Thursday afternoon skills check near Chapel Hill. She will need to bring a rolling demo case, so flight timing and rental-car pickup matter more than usual. From Denver, a Sunday afternoon nonstop into Raleigh-Durham creates a calmer start but adds a hotel night, while a Monday morning itinerary saves a night but leaves little room for delays; one-stop options are cheaper but add connection risk. Hotel areas under consideration include a central Cary suite property, a higher-rated Durham hotel, and an airport-area option that may be less useful once the clinic map is finalized.

events.continuity_hook: This follows the first Research Triangle planning pass once clinic times and locations are firm enough for booking.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the outbound and return flights, pick the hotel, set the rental-car pickup and drop-off windows, and list the room, parking, seat, and demo-case booking steps.
events.scenario_brief: The Research Triangle contacts confirm a Monday 3:30 p.m. setup in Cary, a Tuesday 8:30 a.m. start in Durham, Wednesday sessions in Raleigh, and a Thursday midafternoon wrap near Chapel Hill. That makes the Sunday afternoon nonstop into Raleigh-Durham the safest outbound despite costing more than a Monday one-stop. The hotel shortlist has narrowed to a Cary suite hotel with strong reviews, parking, pool, and fitness access but no hot tub, a Durham extended-stay hotel with better recovery amenities but longer first-day driving, and an airport hotel that is cheapest but poorly placed for the week. Erin also needs to decide whether to return Thursday evening after the wrap or take a calmer Friday morning flight.

events.continuity_hook: This is a narrow post-booking schedule change within the Research Triangle rollout.
events.interaction_goal: Decide whether to move to the later Friday itinerary or add a Saturday return, then note the flight, hotel, rental-car, and client-notification steps for the chosen plan.
events.scenario_brief: After Erin books the Sunday afternoon nonstop, the Cary hotel, the rental car, and a Friday midday return, the Chapel Hill lead asks for a Friday morning debrief that may run until 11:30 a.m. The booked return is now tight once the drive to Raleigh-Durham airport, fuel stop, rental return, and security are included. A later Friday flight is available with a connection, while a Saturday morning nonstop would be easier but adds another hotel night.
